title: The verb avere (to have)
rule: ho, hai, ha, abbiamo, avete, hanno. Possession, and a set of states English expresses with "to be". This page grows as the tenses are taught.

blocks.title: The silent h
blocks.text: Four forms begin with h: [[ho]], [[hai]], [[ha]], [[hanno]]. The h is never pronounced; it exists to tell them apart on paper from [[o|or]], [[ai|to the]], [[a|to]] and [[anno|year]].

head: Use
Example
rows: Ho una moka. Dora ha una casa.
Ho fame / sete / caldo / freddo / sonno.
Ho paura. Ho fretta. Ho bisogno di un caffè.
Ho capito. Ho sentito. Abbiamo mangiato.

items.t: Hai la chiave? — Sì, ce l'ho.
items.n: Do you have the key? — Yes, I've got it.
items.note: ce l'ho: the everyday way to say "I have it"; pronouns in unit 10

items.t: I nonni hanno una casa a Roccamarina.
items.n: The grandparents have a house in Roccamarina.

items.t: Ho freddo. Hai fame? Ha fretta.
items.n: I'm cold. Are you hungry? He / she is in a hurry.

items.why: States of the body take avere.

items.wrong: Ho trenta anni. (spoken as two words)
items.why: Written both ways, but spoken with elision: trent'anni.
Not wrong, but the pronoun at the end adds emphasis you may not want.

items.wrong: A un cane. O una casa.
items.right: Ha un cane. Ho una casa.
items.why: Without the h, these are prepositions and conjunctions.

items.q: Dora e Pasquale ___ sessantotto e settantadue anni.
items.n: Dora and Pasquale are sixty-eight and seventy-two.

items.q: I'm thirsty and I'm in a hurry.
